hourly.summary: The Gunners' faithful are buzzing with quiet confidence — squad building's earning plaudits for long-term vision, a Champions League showdown with Bayern looms as the perfect litmus test, and even the women's team podcasts are keeping supporters up past their bedtime. There's a palpable sense that the project is on the right track, even if the league table still has a few wobbles to iron out.

daily.summary: The day began with weary pragmatism — fans accepting ugly wins but annoyed by 'boring' labels — shifted to anxious grumbling by midday despite 10 wins in 11 and title-favorite status, then hardened into defiant siege mentality by evening: European away-day buzz, transfer optimism, and a circled-wagons fury at media and internal critics alike. Results stay strong; the narrative stays hostile; the tribe chooses 'us against the world.'

weekly.summary: The week began in injury-induced crisis, spiked to euphoria after a statement Champions League win, then crashed violently when the club announced 60 redundancies amid record revenues and a massive Arteta contract — a betrayal narrative that reframed all subsequent on-pitch success. A brief optimistic rebound mid-week faded into conflicted, grudging acceptance as Arsenal topped the table with 'ugly' pragmatic wins, leaving fans torn between results and a gnawing sense that the club's soul has been corporatized. The dominant arc is extreme volatility anchored by a core fracture between sporting dominance and institutional trust.
